title: Dragon Tree: Ancient Dragon Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: Cut the bark and the sap runs dark red, hence the name. Tenerife's Drago Milenario is put near 700 years by one study and over 1,000 by tradition.
intro: Nobody can date a dragon tree, and that is the species rather than sloppy record keeping. Dracaena draco lays down no annual rings, so every age here is an estimate and some are wide open: Tenerife's Drago Milenario is put near 700 years by a modern study and at a thousand or more by tradition, and the tree in the Parque Genoves in Cadiz anywhere between 100 and 200. The name comes from the sap. Cut into the bark and the resin that runs out is dark red, sold across Europe for centuries as dragon's blood, a dye and a medicine. Shape is the other reason to go. An old dragon tree spreads into a low dome of blunt branch tips, and the one at the Quinta Conde dos Arcos in Lisbon is more than twice as wide as it is tall.
